title: Compliance Aids for Eye Drops After Cataract Surgery
official: With or Without Compliance Aids: A Patient-Reported Outcomes Study
summary:
Despite challenges in drop delivery commonly being responsible for treatment failure and medication non-adherence (1), to date only one study has directly compared the safety and efficacy of compliance aids (Autodrop® and Opticare®) to regular bottle use.(23) In Scotland, some of these devices are available free of charge on prescription, although options are limited. Compleye® only fits the Hylo-series bottles, using a pump-type design. Opticare® fits wide-necked bottles due to its collar adaptor, and employs palmar grip strength.

Opticare Arthro 5® and 10® are specifically designed for patients with arthritis and do not fit all bottles. A more versatile recent product, EziDrops® (EziDrops Ltd, Watford, United Kingdom), fits all standard bottles with a nozzle and prevents involuntary blinking during drop delivery. Although it is not available on prescription, it is the cheapest aid to purchase privately (RRP £7.99) and has the potential to address the aforementioned problems. If successful, this may improve patient experience of drop delivery, and promote treatment adherence.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥18 years
2. Listed for cataract surgery
3. Can administer own medication

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Age \<18 years
2. Listed for other type of surgery
3. Unable to administer own medication (including patients requiring district nurses)
4. Cognitively impaired and unable to consent
